clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old female presented with three weeks of right tibial pain triggered by walking and prolonged standing, relieved at rest. Physical examination revealed local tenderness over the anterior and medial mid-right leg with mild swelling, intact neurovascular status, and ability to bear weight. X-ray imaging demonstrated a well-defined intramedullary sclerotic lesion of the mid-tibial shaft with a narrow zone of transition and no fracture line. Subsequent CT scan better illustrated the sclerotic lesion with medullary canal obliteration, and notably showed no sinus, sequestrum, periosteal reaction, or soft tissue component—findings consistent with intramedullary osteosclerosis. The patient was discharged on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications with instructions to adjust physical activity according to pain tolerance.
